chapter: Cee Pee Johnson, Hampton and the Navy band
title: Cee Pee Johnson band members and individual acts
summary: The players of Johnson's band, where everyone had his own song or act, and Royal's boyhood singing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Who else was in Cee Pee C.P. Johnson's band? (inaudible)?
Jack MacVea (PHONETIC) was a baritone saxophone player. That's the guy that wrote "Open the Door, Richard."
(Inaudible). I remember that; that was in the '40s.

Yeah. And my brother played trumpet, Ernie Royal. Had another guy called Red Mack (PHONETIC). He was a very good trumpet player. And let's see, Alton Redd (PHONETIC) was the drummer and Bernard Banks (PHONETIC) was -- Ulysses Banks was the other saxophone player. And Johnny Miller (PHONETIC) was the bass player that went with the King Cole Trio and that's about it. Cee Pee C.P. Johnson, he played tom-toms, bongos and tom-toms and was a very good entertainer, singer-type thing. He did all things -- dance. Was a very good entertainer. We were -- all the guys in the band sang. We did things together. Every guy in the band had to have his own individual song that he could sing and his act that we could do and it was just --
-- a lot of fun. Oh, I sang a lot of things because I used to be a vocalist. I used to sing "Sunny Side of the Street" and things like that in Curtis Moseby's band, when I would sing.
You sang it all the way through? I humming when you were a baby; well, where else did you know you said you had perfect pitch and you were (inaudible). sing?

I used to sing in Curtis Moseby's band. I used to sing the tunes like "Sunny Side of the Street" and things of that era. I was a boy soprano when I was a kid in school and all of a sudden my voice changed and nothing happened after that.
It must have been after that that you (inaudible). were singing with, . . .
Yeah, well, I -- that was secondary, really, I didn't consider myself as being a singer at all. That was just something that could happen.
And so Everybody in the Johnson band. . . .
Everybody in the band had their own act.
Real fun band and a whole lot of talent.
Everybody could sing something and everybody could do something and it was a thing of personal pride with all of us, to have our own thing, you know?
